description: Findings of the two review lenses that failed with an API overload in round 1 and were re-run on the reworked contracts (commit 7a1ec3b..0e52f3f): implementers of sessions 06/07/08 and of sessions 10/11/12. Verbatim reviewer output.

reviewer_summaries.lens:backtest-dash-qa:
Round-2 review from the lens of sessions 10 (Research and Backtesting), 11 (Dashboard) and 12 (QA). Read: MASTER, briefs 00/10/11/12, SHARED_CONTRACTS r2, FIELDS.md, all of gie/core and gie/contracts, conftest, registers, CI, review builder, docs, dependency graph, round-1 dispositions. The repository was being edited while I reviewed (HEAD moved 7a1ec3b -> 0e52f3f); gie/ did not change (git diff 7a1ec3b -- gie is empty) and every counter-example below was run, then re-run at 0e52f3f, with records built from tests/gie/samples.py (consolidated script: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Hello/a1a30857-a87b-5b9c-a837-27f407c26e59/scratchpad/rev_s101112_x7/confirm.py; register experiments ran on scratch copies, nothing in the repository was written).

Verdict: no finding is a blocker in the strict sense (each has a workaround or belongs to a later enforcer), but 17 are major and 3 minor. The round-1 rework added a journal, ledger, gateway and RunManifest whose advertised guarantees do not hold as stated: (1) the look-ahead guard accepts backdated records, is off when no tick is journaled and ignores cross-stream input order; (2) the daily-state validator lets a protected profit floor disappear (claimed fix SF-11 incomplete); (3) FileJournal becomes permanently unreadable after one failed write or a second opener; (4) the gateway wired to the journal's ledger makes the journal refuse ordinary broker reports, and the documented broker-created protective stop cannot pass poll(); (5) a byte-identical journal is impossible because line 0 holds a system-clock reading; (6) run_id binds nothing but (mode, opaque hash, label). For the dashboard, origin and model-validation labels are self-declared and unenforced, there is no read-only/tailing journal reader, and no record exists for current risk state/profit floor, feed or component health, heartbeat cadence or latency. For research, RunManifest cannot separate unconstrained from challenge runs, cannot describe a walk-forward model schedule (max 64 unordered ids), and runs cannot be enumerated for multiplicity. For QA, the registers accept deleted or reworded requirements and 'verified/approved/passing' without real evidence, the evidence files are not bound to a commit, and routing-lock layer 4 plus five further CI gates named in the governance documents do not exist (python -m tools.ci cannot pass at 0e52f3f). Not repeated: items already recorded in CR-003/CR-005 and open items U-01..U-18.
reviewer_summaries.lens:reflex-exec-risk:
Round-2 review, lens = implementer of sessions 06 (Reflex), 07 (Execution), 08 (Risk). Reviewed gie/contracts and gie/core at HEAD 7a1ec3b..0e52f3f (HEAD moved during the review; `git diff 7a1ec3b HEAD -- gie` is empty, so every line number below is valid for both). Every counter-example was built with tests/gie/samples.py and actually run (python3 -B, read-only; nothing in the repository was created or changed). Scripts: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Hello/a1a30857-a87b-5b9c-a837-27f407c26e59/scratchpad/r2_lens_060708/ (helpers.py, r2x_exp1.py, r2x_exp2.py, exp3.py, exp4.py, exp7.py, exp8.py, r2x_exp9.py, r2x_exp10.py, r2x_bench.py). Disclosure: the scratchpad is shared with other running agents; my first scripts used generic names (exp1.py..exp8.py) directly in the scratchpad root and collided with another agent's files of the same names (overwritten in both directions) before I noticed and moved to the private subfolder; no repository file was involved.

Result: 1 blocker, 14 major, 5 minor. None of them is recorded in CR-003/CR-005 or the open items. The single-record invariants are in good shape (stop-out with a gap beyond the stop, rejected orders, limit entry partially filled then cancelled, immediate market fill, exact-floor rejection are all representable). The problems are in the layer added after round 1 - ledger, gateway, journal, sequence validators - when a whole order life is walked through it: (1) a partially filled entry cannot become a Position and its stop cannot follow; (2) the gateway and the journal cannot share the one 'run ledger' the documents describe, and with two ledgers the documented restart re-send is silently swallowed; (3) the broker-created protective stop described in OrderEvent is refused by the gateway; (4) one late duplicate makes poll() lose a batch including fills; (5) the gateway authorises against caller-supplied, possibly stale snapshots and checks reducing orders one by one; (6) order events have three writers but one counter is assumed; (7) ordinary latency races are illegal transitions; (8) fills at or beyond the attached stop cannot be reported. On the risk side the 'floor never decreases' rule is bypassed through a decision without a floor, the surplus rule ignores open exposure and reservations, and neither the daily state nor a reservation's life has a record. Per-tick use: who values positions each tick and how often is undefined, and the journal rule costs about 2 ms per tick with one ratcheting position on the review container (measured, not the owner's hardware). The static live-lock scan named as layer 4 does not exist at the reviewed commit.

findings.area: gie/contracts/journal.py - look-ahead guard (S10-ACC-02, S10-ACC-03, S12-ASG-05)
findings.title: The journal's look-ahead guard accepts backdated records, is switched off when no tick is journaled and does not check input order across streams
findings.detail:
Spec: brief 10 'Acceptance tests: Deterministic replay, no lookahead, tick ordering'; brief 12 'check data leakage'. SHARED_CONTRACTS 6.2 (l.343-359) calls journal order 'causal by construction' and promises 'the look-ahead guard - the market-data watermark of a derived record may not lie beyond the newest tick that was journaled'. Code: journal.py:157-166 compares only the self-declared as_of_time_ns with the max receive time of journaled ticks and returns early when no tick was journaled; the journal has no clock, so decision_time_ns is never compared with anything already journaled; sequence/time checks are per stream only.
Ran (MemoryJournal, samples): (A) manifest only, then S.evidence(decision_time_ns=as_of_time_ns=T0+1 year) -> accepted, journal_seq 1. (B) manifest, tick(recv T0-1ms), tick(seq=1, recv T0+10s), then S.evidence() stamped decision T0 / as_of T0-1ms -> accepted as journal_seq 3: a record published after the later tick claims the earlier watermark and passes CAUSAL-1 and the guard. (C) after the XAUUSD tick received at T0+10s, an XAGUSD tick received at T0-50s is accepted: a mis-merged replay (EventKey order violated) is not refused. The guard also only works if every input tick is journaled, which the text never requires; measured cost of doing so with MemoryJournal: 66 us per publish and >=357 bytes retained per tick besides the tick object (20,000 ticks).
findings.proposed_change: Keep a run watermark in the journal = highest ordering time / EventKey of everything published from the run clock (ticks, order events, Produced records, clock readings); refuse a run-scoped record whose ordering time is below it and a tick whose EventKey is below the last input key (RunManifest and ModelVersion streams exempt). Let the driver advance the watermark with an input marker so the guard does not depend on storing ticks, and fail closed for a Produced record before any input. State in 6.2 that the guard checks declared watermarks only and that the prefix-invariance test remains mandatory. Add these three sequences as tests.

findings.area: gie/contracts/risk_decision.py validate_daily_state_sequence, ledger (G05-06, G05-08; round-1 SF-11)
findings.title: The daily-state sequence check lets a protected profit floor vanish and a halt be bypassed: the claimed fix is incomplete
findings.detail:
Spec: MASTER G05 'Above +5% protect a nondecreasing daily profit floor ... At exactly the floor no new risk.' SHARED_CONTRACTS 9.2: 'Within a trading day an emergency halt stays in force and the profit floor never decreases | validate_daily_state_sequence'; disposition SF-11 'fix'. Code: risk_decision.py:292-297 compares floors only when two consecutive decisions both carry one; ledger.py:87 keys the chain by producer.
Ran (LifecycleLedger, one producer 'risk.gate', same trading day, S.risk_decision): d0 PROFIT_PROTECTION daily_pnl 0.062 floor 0.05 APPROVED -> admitted; d1 (t+10s) NORMAL daily_pnl 0.030 floor None APPROVED risk_frac 0.00104 -> admitted (new risk 2 points below the protected floor); d2 (t+20s) PROFIT_PROTECTION daily_pnl 0.052 floor 0.01 APPROVED -> admitted (floor fell from 0.05 to 0.01). Also: EMERGENCY_HALT rejection by 'risk.gate', then a NORMAL approval by producer 'risk.gate_b' 10 s later on the same day -> admitted. S10's halted-challenge simulations and S12's risk-race tests would rely on this validator.
findings.proposed_change: Track per (run, trading_day) across all risk producers the highest floor seen and whether a halt occurred. Once a floor exists the state may only be PROFIT_PROTECTION or EMERGENCY_HALT, the floor may not be lower than the highest seen, and every approval must satisfy RSK-7/RSK-8 against that highest floor; a halt is sticky for the day for every producer. Add the sequences above as tests.

findings.area: gie/contracts/journal.py FileJournal (G08 persistent state, S07-ACC-08, S12 failure injection)
findings.title: One failed write leaves the in-memory journal ahead of the file and the file permanently unreadable; a second FileJournal on the same path corrupts it
findings.detail:
Spec: MASTER G08 'Persistent state, restart reconciliation'; SHARED_CONTRACTS 6.2 'A refused record leaves the journal unchanged'. Code: journal.py:189-197 admits the record to ledger, tracker, _entries and _positions before _persist(); FileJournal.__init__ (217-226) always opens the file in append mode with no lock.
Ran: FileJournal, publish manifest; replace the handle by one whose first write raises OSError(28 'No space left on device'); publish(S.tick()) raises, but len(journal)=2 with 1 line on disk; retry publish(same tick) -> returns 1 (idempotent hit, nothing written); publish(tick seq 1) -> written as journal_seq 2; reopening the file -> GIE.JOURNAL.CORRUPT 'journal line does not match the record it contains'. Second case: writer w and a second FileJournal r on the same path; r has mode 'ab', does not see w's next record, r.publish(S.evidence()) appends a second journal_seq 2; reopening -> GIE.JOURNAL.CORRUPT. Neither failure is detected when it happens.
findings.proposed_change: Write and fsync the line before mutating in-memory state, or roll back and mark the journal failed (refuse every later publish until reopened) when _persist raises. Take an exclusive lock on the file for the writer. Make the opener injectable so session 12 can inject IO failures, and add both sequences as tests.

findings.area: gie/contracts/guarded.py, ledger.py, journal.py, OrderEvent (S10-ASG-01 'same ... execution interfaces as paper')
findings.title: Wiring the gateway to the journal's ledger makes the journal refuse normal broker reports, and a broker-created protective stop cannot pass OrderGateway.poll
findings.detail:
Docs: guarded.py:55 'the order gateway needs the run's LifecycleLedger'; MemoryJournal exposes .ledger; D-021 'admits the request and every report returned by the adapter to the lifecycle ledger'. Ran with a labelled fixture adapter and samples.order_lifecycle(): gateway built with ledger=journal.ledger; submit ok; journal.publish(SUBMIT_REQUESTED) ok; one poll() returns ACCEPTED, PARTIALLY_FILLED, FILLED; then journal.publish(ACCEPTED) -> GIE.STATE.ILLEGAL_TRANSITION 'no event may follow terminal state FILLED', PARTIALLY_FILLED refused likewise, FILLED -> GIE.SEQ.GAP. With a separate LifecycleLedger all three are accepted, so the natural reading of 'the run's ledger' breaks the commonest case (two reports in one poll).
Second: FIELDS.md OrderEvent: 'The hard stop of a position is its own PROTECTIVE_STOP order, created by the simulated broker from attached_stop_price the instant the entry fills'. OEV-2 makes order_seq 0 a SUBMIT_REQUESTED, and guarded.py:180-183 refuses any request coming from poll. Ran samples.protective_stop_lifecycle(): poll returning [SUBMIT_REQUESTED, ACCEPTED] -> 'an adapter reports broker events, it does not issue requests'; poll returning only ACCEPTED -> 'the first event of an order must be SUBMIT_REQUESTED with order_seq 0'. The documented flow has no path through the only interface between adapter and engine.
findings.proposed_change: Give the gateway the run's RecordSink and let it publish each request and report itself before admitting the next (one ledger, one order), or state that gateway and journal ledgers must be distinct and remove the journal.ledger accessor. For broker-created orders either add a broker-originated first event type or allow poll to return the SUBMIT_REQUESTED of a PROTECTIVE_STOP/TAKE_PROFIT that names the position of the filled entry. Add a golden sequence test 'entry fills, stop order appears' through gateway and journal.

findings.area: RunManifest, SHARED_CONTRACTS 6.2 (S10-ACC-01 deterministic replay)
findings.title: A byte-identical journal is impossible as specified: its first record carries a system-clock reading, and model status is not pinned
findings.detail:
SHARED_CONTRACTS l.349: 'Replaying the same inputs MUST reproduce the journal byte for byte (S01-ACC-08, S07-ACC-08, S10-ACC-01)'. FIELDS.md RunManifest.created_time_ns: 'When the run was created (system clock, also for replays)' (run.py:103-105), and the manifest is journal line 0.
Ran: two MemoryJournals with identical config, tick and evidence, manifests built 5 s apart -> same run_id, canonical_lines() differ at line 0 (different SHA-256). On restart, re-publishing a rebuilt manifest into the reopened FileJournal -> GIE.SEQ.CONFLICT 'a journal belongs to exactly one run'.
Further sources of difference that the text leaves open: Candidate/TradePlan.model_status is 'Promotion status of that model at decision time', but ModelVersion says 'Registry times are always readings of the system clock, never of a replay clock' and RunManifest.model_version_ids pins ids, not registry revisions, so a rerun after a promotion or rollback writes different bytes and 'status at decision time' has no meaning in virtual time. Each of sessions 01, 07, 10 and 12 will therefore define 'identical' differently.
findings.proposed_change: Make created_time_ns null (or a configured value covered by the config hash) for REPLAY, or keep wall-clock creation time outside the journal; alternatively define the determinism comparison normatively (which fields are excluded) and ship one journal_digest() helper used by all sessions. Pin (model_version_id, revision, status) in the manifest and define model_status in replay as the pinned status.

findings.area: RunManifest / identity.run_id / RunContext (S10-DEL-03 configs, S10-DEL-04 seeds, S12-ASG-07)
findings.title: run_id binds only mode, an opaque hash and a label; seed, commit, data, parameters and role can differ under one run_id and the journal does not hold the run to its manifest
findings.detail:
Spec: MASTER 'Record exact commit, files, tests, commands, results'; review gate 'data provenance'; brief 10 deliverables 'configs, seeds'; brief 12 'Verify reports against raw exports and commits'. FIELDS.md claims: 'run_id is derived from the mode, the hash of the complete run configuration and the label, and the manifest verifies it, so a run id cannot be claimed for another configuration'. identity.py:61-75 hashes (mode, config_sha256, label); config_sha256 is a free 64-hex string and no run-configuration document, schema or builder exists.
Ran: S.run_manifest() variants with seed 8 or None, another code_commit, data period +1 year, other data_sources, data_origin HISTORICAL, role PRIMARY, no models, contract_set_version 9.9.9, arbitrary parameters_sha256 -> all valid, all with the same run_id. code_commit has no dirty-tree indicator; data is named by feed id only (no content hash, count or first/last seq). One optional seed covers 'every pseudo-random element' with no derivation rule and RunContext offers no seeded generator. Journal with manifest(data_origin=HISTORICAL, data_sources=('hist_v1',)): a tick from source 'fixture' -> accepted; a tick received one day after data_end_ns -> accepted.
findings.proposed_change: Define the run configuration as a canonical record (journaled after the manifest or nested in it) and compute config_sha256 inside RUN-1 from the manifest's own fields plus that record. Add a code-tree-dirty flag or tree hash, a per-stream data digest (first/last seq, count, SHA-256) and a derive_seed(run_seed, purpose) function in gie.core exposed through RunContext. Let the journal refuse ticks from undeclared sources or outside the declared period.

findings.area: journal / Candidate / RiskDecision / data_origin (S11-ASG-15, S11-ASG-17, S11-ASG-18)
findings.title: Origin and validation labels are self-declared: the journal accepts BROKER_FEED records in a fixture run and ACTIVE candidates for a RESEARCH model
findings.detail:
Spec: brief 11 'Clearly label simulated, unavailable and unvalidated values.' CLAUDE.md rule 4; ARCHITECTURE.md section 3 principle 6 'synthetic fixture data can never be relabelled as market data downstream'. causality.check_derivation is opt-in and the journal never calls it.
Ran: run whose manifest says HISTORICAL and whose only tick is SYNTHETIC_FIXTURE; S.evidence(run_id=m.run_id, data_origin=DataOrigin.BROKER_FEED) -> accepted. Journal with ModelVersion RESEARCH revision 0, then S.candidate(model_status=ModelStatus.ACTIVE) for that model -> accepted; a candidate marked ACTIVE for a model id that is neither in RunManifest.model_version_ids nor registered -> accepted. RiskDecision.quality_validated is equally unchecked. ModelVersion.validated (an ACTIVE model fitted on fixture data is not validated) is not visible on Candidate or TradePlan, so a dashboard working 'from records alone' shows such values as validated market-data results. Open item U-17 (only ACTIVE models may lead to entries in a PRIMARY run) rests on the same unverified field.
findings.proposed_change: Enforce at publication: record.data_origin not better than the manifest's and than the worst tick origin journaled so far; tick.origin not better than the manifest's; a scoring model must be listed in the manifest; model_status and quality_validated must equal the pinned or ledger status. Carry a model_validated flag (or the training data origin) on Candidate and TradePlan.

findings.area: SHARED_CONTRACTS section 10, gie/contracts/interfaces.py, gie/core/clock.py (S10-ASG-01)
findings.title: The run-to-completion step defines tick delivery only; how records reach their consumers is undefined and there is no shared driver or conformance test
findings.detail:
Spec: brief 10 'Build chronological tick replay using same decision/risk/execution interfaces as paper.' Section 10 (l.523-528) orders delivery 'protective -> tactical (risk, decision, execution) -> strategic (evidence, prediction)', while 6.2 (l.347) says 'a whole decision chain shares one instant, which is the normal case in replay'. interfaces.py offers TickSink.on_tick only: no interface delivers Evidence to 04, Candidates to 05 or OrderEvents/Positions to 06/08 (no on_record/subscribe anywhere in gie/). With tactical before strategic, evidence from tick k cannot reach the decision engine in step k unless records cascade inside the step; whether and in which order they cascade decides the journal order, so session 10's replay loop and the coordinator's paper loop (gie.app does not exist yet) can both follow the prose and produce different journals. 'A sink that raises is marked failed' has no API or record.
Related, ran: a component given RunContext(clock=ReplayClock, scheduler=same object) calls ctx.clock.advance_to(now+3600 s) inside on_tick; the clock moved and a timer due at +60 s fired inside the tick handler. Only timer callbacks are prevented from advancing.
findings.proposed_change: Add a RecordListener protocol and a normative cascade rule (records published in a step are delivered to subscribers in a fixed tier order until quiescent, with a bound). Implement one step driver in the foundation used by both replay and paper, with a conformance test that feeds the same inputs through ReplayClock and through PollingScheduler on a scripted clock and compares journals. Hand components a clock view and scheduler facade; only the driver holds advance_to.

findings.area: missing shared record: daily account state (S11-ASG-08, S11-ASG-09, S10-ASG-10, S10-DEL-05, G10-14, G09-08)
findings.title: Risk state, profit floor, daily result and breaches exist only as fields of RiskDecision, that is only when a plan happens to be evaluated
findings.detail: Spec: brief 11 'Show ... open positions, risk states, profit floor'; brief 10 'Report unconstrained research and halted challenge simulations separately', deliverable 'equity curves', acceptance 'daily denominator checks'; MASTER G10 'Report all eligible days ... drawdown, breaches, phase-specific challenge outcomes'; G09 'Reconcile ... daily breach denominators'. FIELDS.md: daily_state, daily_pnl_frac, profit_floor_frac and reference_equity_amount are RiskDecision fields; no other contract carries account equity or daily state. A halt reached through the loss of an open position without a new plan produces no record; a day without candidates produces no record at all, so day denominators, breach counts and an equity curve cannot be derived from the journal, and the dashboard cannot show the current state between evaluations. CR-003 lists CX-05 AccountSnapshot as 'equity, margin, account-wide positions including other systems', required only before S05 and S06 (dependency_graph.yaml:99-101); daily state, floor and breach are not named and S10/S11 are not consumers.
findings.proposed_change: Extend the recorded scope of CX-05 (or add a DailyAccountState record): trading_day, daily_state, daily_pnl_frac, profit_floor_frac, equity, reference equity, breach flags; emitted on every state change, at each trading-day boundary including days without trades, and periodically. Name S10, S11 and S12 as consumers and tie its sequence rules to the floor/halt validator.

findings.area: missing shared records: health, errors, heartbeat, latency (S11-ASG-10, S11-ASG-11, S11-ACC-02, S12-ASG-03, S12-ACC-02, S12-ACC-03, G03-10)
findings.title: Errors 'are data' but cannot be journaled, and no record or interface carries feed status, component failure, heartbeat cadence or measured latency
findings.detail:
Spec: brief 11 'Show ... data freshness, latency' and acceptance 'stale/disconnect state'; brief 12 'run mutation/failure injection, stress concurrency and latency', acceptance 'restart/disconnect, stale feed'; MASTER G03 'measure p50/p95/p99/max and end-to-end delays', G08 'disconnect/stale-feed fail closed'. SHARED_CONTRACTS l.293: 'Errors are data. GieError.to_dict() is the journal form. Errors are never swallowed'; section 10: 'A sink that raises is marked failed'.
Ran: journal.publish(StaleDataError(...).to_dict()), publish of the error object and publish(LatencyRecorder(...).summary()) all end in AttributeError "type object 'dict' has no attribute 'CONTRACT'" (not a GieError); the registry holds the ten contracts only. ClockReading is described as 'the data form used for heartbeats and for the dashboard's data-freshness display' but no producer, cadence or parameter is defined; with a silent feed nothing is published, so a reader of the journal cannot tell feed silence from a dead process. Section 3.2 says measured latency 'never enters a record' and no other transport exists. None of CX-01..CX-09 covers any of this, so injected failures are not observable in the run history.
findings.proposed_change: Record as contract extensions owned by session 00: a HealthEvent/ErrorEvent record (component, GieError code and details, FAILED/RECOVERED, feed CONNECTED/SILENT/DISCONNECTED), a heartbeat rule (who publishes ClockReading, cadence as a research parameter) and a latency summary record on a side stream excluded from determinism comparison. Make to_wire raise UnknownContractError for a non-record.

findings.area: RunManifest.role, RecordSource, gie/core/params.py (S10-ASG-10, G10-05, G10-07, G10-15, G10-17)
findings.title: Runs cannot be classified as unconstrained research, halted challenge simulation or untouched forward test, nor enumerated for multiplicity
findings.detail: Spec: brief 10 'Report unconstrained research and halted challenge simulations separately.' MASTER G10 'multiple-testing correction ... untouched forward paper ... phase-specific challenge outcomes ... No cherry-picking.' run.py:26-37: RunRole is PRIMARY / SHADOW / RESEARCH; no field states whether daily limits were enforced, which challenge phase was simulated, or that a period is a holdout. Role is not part of run_id (ran: role PRIMARY and RESEARCH with the same config give the same run_id). params.py:126-151 requires all four daily levels, each within (-1, 1) and ordered, so an unconstrained run can only be faked with extreme thresholds and is then visible only through parameters_sha256. RecordSource (interfaces.py:79-88) is single-run and no run catalogue or journal location convention exists, so the number of configurations tried and which periods were already replayed is not derivable from shared infrastructure; reruns of one configuration share a run_id.
findings.proposed_change: Add to RunManifest a risk_regime (UNCONSTRAINED / CHALLENGE_RULES), challenge_phase, experiment_id with trial_index and a holdout flag, and include role and these fields in the run identity. Define an append-only RunCatalog protocol (list manifests) owned by session 00 and used by 09, 10, 11 and 12.

findings.area: RunManifest.model_version_ids, model_version.is_out_of_sample (S10-ACC-07, G10-01, G10-02)
findings.title: A walk-forward model schedule cannot be described (unordered set, at most 64 ids, no validity intervals) and nothing checks that a scoring model is out of sample
findings.detail:
Spec: MASTER G10 'Chronological purged walk-forward, embargo, training-only transforms'; brief 10 acceptance 'purged walk-forward'. run.py:89-99: model_version_ids has max_items=64 and is canonically sorted; the doc defers the schedule to 'the configuration', which is only a hash.
Ran: S.run_manifest with 65 model ids -> 'model_version_ids: must have 0..64 items' (weekly refits over two years need 104 fold models, per model kind); with 3 ids the order given is replaced by id order. Leak that passes every check: S.model_version(training_information_end_ns=T0+30 days); is_out_of_sample(S.candidate().as_of_time_ns, model) returns False; the journal accepts the registry entry and the candidate at T0 scored by that model. is_out_of_sample (model_version.py:470-479) is called by nothing. Splitting a replay into one run per fold to stay under 64 breaks positions, daily state and equity across fold boundaries.
findings.proposed_change: Replace the id set by a model schedule: entries of model_version_id, registry revision, valid_from_ns, valid_until_ns, with a limit that fits walk-forward (or held in the run-configuration record). In REPLAY let the journal refuse, or force a visible IN_SAMPLE marking on, a candidate whose model is not scheduled for its as_of_time_ns or is not out of sample. Publish the split specification as a record, not only a hash.

findings.area: RecordSource / FileJournal (S11-DEP-01, S11-ASG-16, S11-ACC-01, S11-ACC-04)
findings.title: There is no read-only or tailing journal reader: the only RecordSource implementations are writers that load the whole file and fail on an in-flight line
findings.detail:
Spec: brief 11 'Dependencies: 00; read-only contracts from all modules', 'No direct order route', acceptance 'Replay UI with real event payloads; ... no blocking of reflex'. interfaces.py:79-88 RecordSource is implemented only by MemoryJournal and FileJournal, which also expose publish() and the ledger. FileJournal.__init__ (journal.py:217-226) reads the complete file into memory, replays it through every check and opens it for append.
Ran: a second FileJournal used as reader has handle mode 'ab'; after the writer publishes another record the reader still has 2 entries (no follow); a reader opening a file whose last line is still being written -> GIE.JOURNAL.CORRUPT 'journal ends with an incomplete line (torn write)'; the reader's own publish corrupts the file (see the durability finding). The dashboard rule in dependency_graph.yaml ('dashboard.gie ... read_only: true') is to be enforced by tools/check_architecture.py, which does not exist, and gie.contracts exports GuardedExecutionAdapter and both journals to any importer.
findings.proposed_change: Provide a JournalReader implementing RecordSource only: opens read-only, follows appended lines incrementally, treats an incomplete last line as not yet published, verifies fingerprints, does not keep all entries in memory. Provide a read-only view of MemoryJournal and a narrow import surface for the dashboard that contains no gateway, adapter or sink.

findings.area: tools/gie_registers.py, specifications/requirements_matrix.yaml (S12-ASG-01, S12-DEL-01, D-015)
findings.title: Requirements can be deleted or reworded, and set to verified and approved with an unrelated file as evidence, while register validation stays green
findings.detail:
Spec: brief 12 'Independently verify requirements'; matrix header 'Never delete a requirement; change status only with evidence'; D-015 'no requirement can disappear, no status verified without an existing evidence file'. Code: gie_registers.py:823-831 only compares the count with minimum_requirement_count, an optional key of the same file; 656-662 only checks that source_clause is not empty; 696-705 accepts any existing repository path as evidence; review_status has no rule.
Ran on scratch copies with the repository's tool: (1) removed S12-ASG-05 'Check data leakage' and G10-17 'No cherry-picking', set the minimum to 582, changed the text of S12-ASG-06 to 'Check documentation.' and the source_clause of S12-ASG-07 to 'Anything.' -> 'registers valid: 582 requirements', exit 0. findings.area: OrderEvent fills (S10-ACC-02, S10-ACC-04, G09-10, S12-ASG-07)
findings.title: A fill cannot be traced to the quote it was matched against, so execution look-ahead and realised costs cannot be verified from records
findings.detail:
Spec: brief 10 acceptance 'no lookahead ... costs'; MASTER G09 'Use actual tick data for fast execution claims'. OrderEvent carries event and receive time, last_fill_price and last_fill_cost_amount but no watermark and no tick reference; reference_price is mandatory for entries only; it is not a Produced record, so the journal's guard does not apply to it.
Ran: journal with one tick (bid 2650.10 / ask 2650.35 received at T0-1ms), then samples.order_lifecycle(): a BUY LIMIT at 2649.80 is PARTIALLY_FILLED at 2649.80 at T0+1s and FILLED at 2649.78 at T0+2s -> all accepted although no journaled quote ever reached those prices. Realised spread and slippage per fill cannot be separated from commission with the recorded fields.
findings.proposed_change: Add to fill events the stream and seq of the matched tick (or a watermark plus the executable bid/ask at the fill), make reference_price mandatory for every MARKET and EXIT request, let the journal refuse a fill whose watermark lies beyond the newest input, and give QA a helper that re-prices fills against the tick store.

findings.area: canonical JSON for the dashboard (S11-ACC-01; beyond the owner's wording, which names no browser technology)
findings.title: A browser's JSON.parse silently changes nanosecond instants; no display projection or tested JavaScript decoder is specified
findings.detail: SHARED_CONTRACTS l.385-389 notes that 'JavaScript consumers need a BigInt-aware parser' and that float fields 'may appear as integer literals'. Ran with Node 22 on to_json(samples.tick()): receive_time_ns 1795685399999000000 is read as 1795685399999000064; a second tick 100 ns later parses to the same number (two distinct instants collapse); Number.isSafeInteger is false. TradePlan.expected_net_r = 1.0 is written as the token 1, so a BigInt-aware parser cannot tell float from integer fields without the schema; decimals arrive as strings (bid + ask evaluates to '2650.12650.35'). findings.area: Position / OrderEvent - partial fills (S07-ASG-03, S07-ACC-02, G04-12)
findings.title: A partially filled entry cannot be represented as a Position, and its protective stop cannot follow the fills
findings.detail: Brief 07: "Implement paper/replay order state machine, market/limit/stop orders, partial fills, cancel/replace, multiple positions, idempotency, persistence, restart reconciliation and simulated broker-side protection." Master G04: "Hard protective stops". gie/contracts/position.py:292-297 makes initial_volume_lots, average_entry_price and initial_risk_amount immutable for GIE positions, :348-349 refuses any volume increase, and :64-65 derives exactly one position id per entry order, so later fills of the same order cannot become a second position either. Counter-example run with samples.order_lifecycle() (PARTIALLY_FILLED 0.20, then FILLED 0.50): Position revision 0 for 0.20 lots is admitted by LifecycleLedger; revision 1 after the second fill raises IllegalTransitionError in all three variants tried: 'initial_volume_lots may not change during the life of a GIE position'; (initial volume declared 0.50 up front) 'volume_lots may not increase (no averaging down, no adding to a position)'; (volume kept, price updated) 'average_entry_price may not change'. The stop cannot follow: REPLACE_REQUESTED volume 0.20 -> 0.50 raises 'volume_lots may not increase' (order_event.py:532-533) and a second stop for the added 0.30 raises 'a protective stop covers the whole open volume' (authorization.py:114-115). So either no Position and no stop order exist while an entry is PARTIALLY_FILLED (the fixture position_lifecycle() itself opens the position only at the FILLED instant, one second after the first fill), or the simulator may never partially fill an entry. D-012 / U-12 record 'volume never increases' as an interpretation of 'no averaging down' but not this collision with the second fill of the same approved order.
findings.proposed_change: Separate 'fills of the opening order' from 'adding to a position': while the opening ENTRY order is not terminal, allow volume_lots, initial_volume_lots, average_entry_price and initial_risk_amount to grow up to the order's cumulative fill (the ledger holds the entry order's newest event, so validate_position_transition can check volume <= cumulative_filled_lots <= granted volume) and freeze them once the order is terminal. In the same phase allow the PROTECTIVE_STOP volume to rise to the position volume (or make the stop position-attached without its own volume). Add a golden sequence and a test for submit -> partial -> partial -> filled and for partial -> cancel.

findings.area: LifecycleLedger wiring: GuardedExecutionAdapter + journal (S07-ASG-06/07/08, S07-ACC-05, G08-07)
findings.title: With the one 'run ledger' the documents describe, orders are silently never sent or fills cannot be journaled; with two ledgers the documented restart re-send is swallowed
findings.detail: SHARED_CONTRACTS.md:474-476: sequence rules are "enforced by the LifecycleLedger, through which every journal and the order gateway admit records"; guarded.py:54-55 demands "the run's LifecycleLedger"; journal.py:83 creates one per journal and :102-104 exposes it as journal.ledger. Runs with the gateway given journal.ledger: (a) request journaled first (write-ahead), then gateway.submit(entry, plan=, decision=) returns normally and the adapter was never called (adapter calls: []), because guarded.py:142-143 treats a request the ledger already knows as an 'identical repeat'; (b) gateway first, then poll() returns ACCEPTED + PARTIALLY_FILLED of one order (the normal result for a marketable order): journal.publish(ACCEPTED) raises 'order_seq must increase by exactly 1' because the gateway already advanced the shared chain, and the next publish raises SequenceGapError. With two separate ledgers both flows work, but after a restart a fresh gateway ledger refuses the first report of every pre-crash order ('the first event of an order must be SUBMIT_REQUESTED with order_seq 0'), and once it is rebuilt from journal.read() the re-send that docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:171 prescribes ("a restarted component can re-send what it is unsure about") is dropped before the adapter: adapter calls: [], order stays PENDING_SUBMIT. Nothing in the specification says which wiring is meant.
findings.proposed_change: Specify the wiring normatively and test the crash points. Suggested: one ledger per run; the gateway performs admission, and journal.publish accepts (in order) records that the ledger has already admitted instead of re-validating them against a chain that has moved on; the gateway always forwards a re-sent known *_REQUESTED event to the adapter (ExecutionAdapter is already documented as idempotent per order_event_id, interfaces.py:137-139) and only skips the ledger admit; define the write-ahead order request -> journal -> adapter -> reports -> journal.

findings.area: OrderEvent / gateway / Position - broker-side protection (S07-ASG-09, G08-08, G04-12)
findings.title: The PROTECTIVE_STOP 'created by the simulated broker' cannot enter the system, and a position without a working stop cannot be reported
findings.detail: order_event.py:257-260: "The hard stop of a position is its own PROTECTIVE_STOP order, created by the simulated broker from attached_stop_price the instant the entry fills". But guarded.py:180-184 refuses any request event coming out of poll(), and order_event.py:597-599 with OEV-2 refuses an order whose first event is not SUBMIT_REQUESTED. Run: after gateway.submit(entry), poll() returning the entry's reports followed by samples.protective_stop_lifecycle()[0:2] raises 'an adapter reports broker events, it does not issue requests'; reporting only the stop's ACCEPTED raises 'the first event of an order must be SUBMIT_REQUESTED with order_seq 0'. The same holds for attached_take_profit_price and for any broker-initiated close (margin stop-out, weekend closure): there is no order that could carry the fill. If instead the engine submits the stop after it has seen the fill, the position has no stop order for the request latency, and a stop-out in the same burst has no order to be reported on. Meanwhile POS-3 (position.py:66) forces stop_price to be non-null while OPEN, whereas the ledger admits REJECTED, CANCELED and EXPIRED on a working PROTECTIVE_STOP (run: broker-initiated CANCELED and EXPIRED both admitted, although SHARED_CONTRACTS.md:457 says "a protective stop never does" expire), so snapshots must keep asserting a stop that is not working - unknown is not reported as unknown.
findings.proposed_change: Decide who originates protection orders and write it down once. Either let the adapter originate non-ENTRY orders (poll() accepts a first event of a PROTECTIVE_STOP / TAKE_PROFIT / broker EXIT whose position_id derives from an entry order the ledger shows as filled), or state that the engine submits them in the step of the fill and that the simulator enforces attached_stop_price until the order is accepted. Add a protection status to Position (client_order_id of the working stop, or UNPROTECTED with reason) and refuse EXPIRED for intent PROTECTIVE_STOP in validate_order_transition.

findings.area: GuardedExecutionAdapter.poll / duplicates (S07-ACC-01, S07-DEL-04)
findings.title: One late duplicate or faulty report makes poll() discard the whole batch, including fills already admitted to the ledger
findings.detail: Brief 07 acceptance tests: "Duplicate messages, partial fill races, rejected orders, reconnect, crash recovery". guarded.py:171-186 drains the adapter, admits each event and lets an exception abort without returning anything; ledger.py:110-111 treats only a repeat of the newest event of a chain as idempotent. Run: after ACCEPTED and PARTIALLY_FILLED were processed, poll() receives [re-delivered ACCEPTED (order_seq 1), FILLED (order_seq 3)] -> IllegalTransitionError 'order_seq must increase by exactly 1'; nothing is returned, the adapter queue is empty and the ledger still shows PARTIALLY_FILLED: the FILLED report is lost. In the run of the previous finding the entry's ACCEPTED / PARTIALLY_FILLED / FILLED were admitted to the ledger (state FILLED) but never returned to the engine because a later element of the batch raised, so engine and journal never see a fill the ledger already contains. A duplicate of the newest event is handled correctly (returned n=2), which shows the gap is the older duplicate.
findings.proposed_change: Classify per event instead of failing the batch: keep the fingerprint per (client_order_id, order_seq); an event at an already admitted order_seq with identical content is a duplicate and is dropped (counted), different content is a conflict. Return the admitted events together with a per-event error list (result object), so nothing behind a bad event is lost and nothing admitted is withheld. Add the duplicate, reordered and conflicting cases as tests.

findings.area: authorization.validate_reducing_order / gateway (SHARED_CONTRACTS 9.3, G04-09, G04-10)
findings.title: The gateway authorises against whatever Position or plan snapshot the caller hands in and checks each reducing order in isolation
findings.detail: SHARED_CONTRACTS.md:499-502: "every other order needs the open GIE position it belongs to and may only reduce it". guarded.py:112-120 and :141 pass the caller's `position` to validate_reducing_order without comparing it with the ledger, and authorization.py:107-111 compares each order's volume with that snapshot only. Runs: (a) the gateway's own ledger holds the position as CLOSED (revision 2); gateway.submit(EXIT SELL 0.50, position=<revision 0, OPEN>) is forwarded to the adapter - a sell with no position behind it, i.e. new exposure without plan or approval; (b) for one 0.50 position a second EXIT 0.50 (attempt 1), a TAKE_PROFIT 0.50 and a second PROTECTIVE_STOP 0.50 (attempt 1 while attempt 0 is WORKING) are all accepted, and the redundant stop can then not be cancelled ('the protective stop of an open position may not be cancelled', authorization.py:135-136); (c) after a WITHDRAWN revision 1 of the plan was admitted to the ledger, gateway.submit(entry, plan=<revision 0 SELECTED>, decision=<its approval>) is forwarded, although trade_plan.py:195-198 says a new revision voids the approval. Nothing states that a fill of a non-ENTRY order is clamped to the open volume, and a flipped position could not even be recorded (POS-3 needs plan and opening entry).
findings.proposed_change: Let the gateway look the position and the newest plan revision up in the run ledger (or verify that the supplied snapshot equals the ledger's newest). Give validate_reducing_order the other open reducing orders of the position and enforce: at most one non-terminal PROTECTIVE_STOP, sum of working EXIT and TAKE_PROFIT volume <= open volume, a redundant stop may be cancelled while another covers the position. State reduce-only semantics normatively: a non-ENTRY fill never exceeds the open volume, the remainder is cancelled.

findings.area: OrderEvent streams, seq, attempt - reflex vs execution (S06-ASG-01, S07-ASG-06)
findings.title: Order events have three writers (execution, reflex, simulator) but the validators assume one stream, one counter and one attempt numbering
findings.detail: SHARED_CONTRACTS.md:34 lists OrderEvent as produced by "07 execution" only, the diagram at :43 shows "06 reflex (per tick) ----+ protective orders only" writing OrderEvents, and interfaces.py:159-160 calls the gateway "What the execution and reflex engines depend on to place orders". order_event.py:617-619 requires `seq` - the position in stream order_event/<producer> - not to decrease between consecutive events of one order, while `producer` is not in ORDER_IMMUTABLE_FIELDS (:482-497). Run: stop order events from producer execution.sim (seq 4, 5); REPLACE_REQUESTED from producer reflex.engine with its own stream position seq 0 -> IllegalTransitionError 'seq may not decrease'; the same request with seq 9 is admitted - acceptance depends on two unrelated counters. client_order_id of a non-entry order is f(run, position, intent, attempt) (identity.py:171-185): when reflex and execution each number their first EXIT for a position 'attempt 0' they obtain the same id and the second is refused with 'order_seq must increase by exactly 1' (run). To build any request the reflex engine must also hold the order's newest event, because every event repeats all parameters and needs the next order_seq.
findings.proposed_change: Choose one model and state it in section 1. (a) Single writer: the reflex engine expresses intents through a small protocol in gie.contracts.interfaces (tighten_stop(position_id, trigger_price, reason), exit(position_id, volume, reason)) and execution builds, numbers and journals the OrderEvent; or (b) several writers: compare seq only between events of the same producer, give each writer its own attempt namespace, and add a ledger accessor 'working protective stop of position X'. Add a test with two producers.

findings.area: ORDER_TRANSITIONS / validate_order_transition - races (S07-ASG-04, S07-ASG-14, S07-ACC-02)
findings.title: The order state machine refuses ordinary latency races between requests and reports
findings.detail: Brief 07: "partial fills, cancel/replace ... Model bid/ask, costs, slippage, latency"; acceptance: "partial fill races". Table order_event.py:88-123, time rule :617-619. Runs: (1) SUBMIT_REQUESTED, then CANCEL_REQUESTED while PENDING_SUBMIT (allowed, :97), then the acknowledgement that was already under way: ACCEPTED -> 'PENDING_CANCEL --ACCEPTED--> WORKING is not allowed' (with order_state PENDING_CANCEL the record itself violates OEV-3); REJECTED(MARKET_CLOSED) -> 'PENDING_CANCEL --REJECTED--> REJECTED is not allowed'. With any modelled acknowledgement latency this is the normal outcome of a cancel inside that window. (2) A fill that happened at the broker 2 ms before GIE created the cancel request and is observed 3 ms after it -> 'event_time_ns may not decrease', although the comment at :109 says "Fills can race with a pending cancel or replace". (3) PENDING_REPLACE --CANCEL_REQUESTED--> PENDING_CANCEL is allowed (:118), but afterwards REPLACED and REPLACE_REJECTED are both not in the table and OEV-14 drops the requested_* values, so the outcome of the outstanding replace cannot be reported. (4) A second, tighter REPLACE_REQUESTED while one is pending is refused ('PENDING_REPLACE --REPLACE_REQUESTED--> PENDING_REPLACE is not allowed'): a per-tick ratchet is limited to one change per broker round trip. That may be intended, but it is stated nowhere and it decides how brief 06's "fast giveback protection" must work.
findings.proposed_change: Add (PENDING_CANCEL, ACCEPTED) -> PENDING_CANCEL, (PENDING_CANCEL, REJECTED) -> REJECTED, (PENDING_CANCEL, REPLACED) and (PENDING_CANCEL, REPLACE_REJECTED) -> PENDING_CANCEL. Require monotonic receive_time_ns only; allow the event_time_ns of a broker report to be earlier than a preceding GIE request. State the single-pending-replace rule and what the reflex engine does meanwhile (coalesce to the newest target; EXIT when protection cannot wait). Add one golden trace per race.

findings.area: OEV-11 / POS-4 - gap and slippage at entry (S07-ASG-13, S07-ASG-14, S06-ACC-02, G05-09)
findings.title: A fill at or beyond the attached stop cannot be reported, and the position it opens cannot exist
findings.detail: Brief 07: "Model bid/ask, costs, slippage, latency and broker constraints"; brief 06 acceptance: "gap/slippage"; master G05: "Slippage can breach floors." order_event.py:167-184 (OEV-11) checks the attached stop against average_fill_price; position.py:76-85 (POS-4) requires the initial stop strictly on the losing side of average_entry_price. Runs: BUY LIMIT 2649.80 with stop 2647.80, gap-down fill at 2647.00 (better than the limit, below the stop) -> OEV-11 violated; BUY MARKET, reference 2650.35, stop 2650.05, filled after modelled latency at 2649.95, or exactly at 2650.05 -> OEV-11 violated; Position with entry 2647.00 and initial stop 2647.80 -> POS-4 violated. The simulator must therefore reject, re-price or drop such fills; each choice changes costs and P&L and none is specified, so sessions 07 and 10 will differ. (Stop-out of an open position with a gap beyond the stop is representable: PROTECTIVE_STOP trigger 2649.90 FILLED at 2641.10 and a CLOSED position with loss 439 against initial risk 104 both construct.)
findings.proposed_change: Keep the geometry check for requests (order price, reference price) but not for fill events, and allow a Position whose entry is at or beyond its stop (it is closed by the stop in the same step with the loss recorded); or state normatively that the simulated broker rejects such an entry with a reason code and that limit orders fill at the limit price. One rule, with gap fixtures in the contract tests.

findings.area: Position valuation per tick - reflex / execution / risk (S06-ASG-01, S06-ASG-02, G03, G04-13)
findings.title: Who values open positions on each tick, in which order and how often is undefined; the high-water mark is tied to snapshot cadence
findings.detail: Master G03: "Reflex every tick"; G04: "fast monotonic profit ratchet based on executable net P&L"; brief 06: "Implement deterministic per-tick protective decisions, executable net P&L peak tracking, monotonic stops, fast giveback protection". SHARED_CONTRACTS.md:35 makes 07 the only producer of Position; :525-526 delivers an input "in the order protective (reflex, simulated broker) -> tactical (risk, decision, execution)", so the snapshot for tick N is produced after the reflex engine has decided on tick N. position.py:100-110 says peak_net_pnl_amount "drives the profit ratchet", and :336-340 allows a new peak to be dated only with the decision time of the snapshot that carries it. Run: a snapshot at T0+60 s reporting a peak of 146 reached on the tick of T0+30 s -> 'a new peak is stamped with the decision time of the snapshot that reached it'; the same peak stamped T0+60 s (the wrong instant) is accepted. So either 07 journals a snapshot per open position on every tick (cost: see the journal finding), or 06 keeps its own tick-level peak that differs from the contract's, and 08 needs a third valuation for the daily state. There is no shared valuation function, and no rule says how records produced inside a step (fills, snapshots, approvals) reach 06 and 08 - only TickSink and the pull interface RecordSource exist - nor whether they arrive in the same step or one tick later.
findings.proposed_change: Put one pure valuation function into gie.contracts (position, tick, instrument spec, cost model -> executable net P&L) used by 06, 07 and 08. Define the snapshot cadence (on every state change and on every new peak/trough, or every tick) and let peak_time_ns be the receive time of the tick that made the peak. Fix the order inside a step (broker fills -> position update -> reflex, or state the one-tick lag explicitly) and add a record-delivery protocol next to TickSink.

findings.area: RiskDecision / validate_daily_state_sequence (G05-06, G05-08, S08-ASG-06, S08-ASG-07, S08-DEL-03, G08-04)
findings.title: The daily profit floor can be dropped and re-set lower within a day, the chain is keyed by producer name, and the daily state exists only inside plan evaluations
findings.detail: Master G05: "Above +5% protect a nondecreasing daily profit floor ... At exactly the floor no new risk." SHARED_CONTRACTS.md:487 claims "Within a trading day an emergency halt stays in force and the profit floor never decreases". risk_decision.py:292-297 compares floors only when both consecutive decisions carry one, RSK-6 (:216-220) forces the floor to null outside PROFIT_PROTECTION, and ledger.py:86-87 keys the chain by `producer`. Runs, all on one trading day: d1 PROFIT_PROTECTION, floor 0.05, pnl 0.062 -> d2 NORMAL, pnl 0.049 (below that floor), no floor, APPROVED -> d3 PROFIT_PROTECTION, floor 0.02, approving risk_frac 0.029: all three admitted (the direct step 0.05 -> 0.02 is refused, so the rule is bypassed only through the intermediate decision). EMERGENCY_HALT from producer risk.gate followed by an APPROVED NORMAL decision from producer risk.gate_b: admitted. reference_equity_amount 100000 -> 1000000 within the day (risk_frac shrinks tenfold): admitted. Because state, floor and reference equity are recorded only as a by-product of a plan evaluation, a restart rebuilds the floor from the last decision (possibly none since +5 % was crossed), crossings of -2 % / -1.75 % / -3 % / +5 % leave no record, and brief 08's deliverable "state traces" has no carrier. CX-05 (AccountSnapshot) as recorded lists equity, margin and positions, not the daily state.
findings.proposed_change: Carry the day's floor on every decision once it has been established and apply RSK-7 / RSK-8 in every state; key the sequence check by (run, trading_day), not by producer; freeze reference_equity_amount within a trading day. Add a DailyRiskState record (trading day, state, daily P&L amount and fraction, floor, reference equity, cause of the transition) emitted on every transition and after a restart - inside CX-05 or as its own contract - and run the validator on that stream.

findings.area: RiskDecision RSK-8 and aggregate fields (G05-07, G04-02..07, S08-ASG-01..04)
findings.title: Above the floor an approval may ignore open exposure and other reservations, and every aggregate may be null on an approval
findings.detail: Master G05: "exceptional setups only with surplus risk budget after costs and open exposure"; G04: "aggregate gross/net and correlated risk, pending orders, margin, costs and gap stress". SHARED_CONTRACTS.md:462 presents RSK-7 / RSK-8 as the encoding of G05-07, but risk_decision.py:56-60 checks only risk_frac <= daily_pnl_frac - profit_floor_frac. Runs: PROFIT_PROTECTION, pnl 0.062, floor 0.05 (surplus 1200 on 100000) with open_risk_amount 1200 and pending_risk_amount 1200 already outstanding and a new approval of risk 1200 -> the record constructs; an approval with equity, open risk, pending risk, margin and gap stress all null -> constructs; margin_required_amount 5000 with margin_free_amount 100 -> constructs. Two approvals evaluated at the same instant can each satisfy RSK-8 and jointly exceed the surplus; the only field that could show it, pending_risk_amount, is optional.
findings.proposed_change: In PROFIT_PROTECTION require open_risk_amount and pending_risk_amount and check risk_amount + open + pending <= surplus amount. On every approval require the aggregates the specification names (open risk, pending risk, margin required and free, gap stress) to be non-null and margin_required_amount <= margin_free_amount (fail closed on unknown). If these are meant to be engine rules only, remove the claim from section 9.1.

findings.area: RiskGate protocol / reservations (S08-ACC-06, S08-ASG-03, G08-04)
findings.title: A reservation has no life after the approval: no record of consumption, partial use, release or expiry, and a released approval can still be spent
findings.detail: Brief 08 acceptance: "simultaneous reservations atomic"; assignment: "pending risk". interfaces.py:110-122: evaluate(plan) reserves and release(reservation_id) "returns an unused reservation; it is idempotent" - nothing else. No contract records a release, so pending_risk_amount of later decisions (risk_decision.py:156-160) cannot be re-derived from the journal by QA or after a restart. Undefined: who calls release (decision or execution) and when; what happens to the unfilled remainder of an entry that is partially filled and then cancelled (release takes no amount); whether the risk engine turns a reservation into open risk by consuming the OrderEvents of the citing entry; whether an entry replace that lowers the volume frees risk. validate_entry_authorization (authorization.py:30-79) accepts any approved, unexpired decision and has no input from which it could learn that the reservation was released (by inspection; there is no record to build a counter-example from).
findings.proposed_change: Add a reservation record (RESERVED -> CONSUMED(amount) / RELEASED(amount, reason) / EXPIRED) emitted by 08 and journaled; state that 08 derives consumption from the OrderEvents of the entry order that cites the decision; give release() a reason code; let the ledger or the gateway refuse an entry whose reservation is no longer RESERVED. Define the test form of 'atomic': two evaluations in one step, the second decision's pending_risk_amount includes the first reservation.

findings.area: ExecutionAdapter protocol / RECONCILED / ledger accessors (S07-ASG-08, S07-ACC-04, S07-ACC-05, G08-05)
findings.title: Restart reconciliation has no query on the adapter, and RECONCILED cannot express three of its normal outcomes
findings.detail: Master G08: "Persistent state, restart reconciliation, disconnect/stale-feed fail closed, idempotent orders". docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:171-174 describes reconciliation as "re-read the journal, compare with the simulated broker, emit RECONCILED events". interfaces.py:125-155 and core/routing_lock.py:69 fix the adapter to submit, cancel, replace, on_tick, poll, open_positions: there is no way to ask for the broker's orders or for one order's state, and no way for the adapter to say when its next report becomes available. Reports with modelled latency must be delivered at their receive time: publishing an ACCEPTED stamped T0+7 ms when polled at T0+2 ms makes the next request at T0+4 ms fail with 'receive_time_ns may not decrease' (run), so the engine needs a timer it cannot derive from the protocol. Runs on RECONCILED: an order that exists at the broker but not in the journal cannot be adopted (as first event: OEV-2 violated; as order_seq 1: 'the first event of an order must be SUBMIT_REQUESTED'); an order the journal holds as EXPIRED but that had filled cannot be corrected ('no event may follow terminal state EXPIRED'); a fill discovered by reconciliation cannot carry its cost (last_fill_cost_amount on RECONCILED -> OEV-9 violated; without it the event is admitted). LifecycleLedger exposes admit, check, group_entry_order, model, open_orders, order, position - no enumeration of open positions, plans or approvals, so state is rebuilt by scanning the whole journal; positions returned by gateway.open_positions() bypass the ledger (guarded.py:188-195).
findings.proposed_change: Add open_orders() / order_status(client_order_id) and next_report_time_ns() (or a wake-up callback) to ExecutionAdapter, ADAPTER_METHODS and the gateway. Allow RECONCILED as the first event of an adopted order and as a correction after a locally recorded EXPIRED / CANCELED when fills are discovered, with fill cost fields. Add ledger.open_positions() and a snapshot / restore pair. Write the reconciliation procedure per crash point into the contract specification.

findings.area: Journal in the tick path (G03-07, G03-08, S06-ASG-07, S06-ACC-06, S07-ACC-05)
findings.title: The journal rule does not fit the proposed tick budget with the reference implementation, and restart cost grows with the whole history
findings.detail: Master G03: "Proposed local targets: tick processing <1 ms, protection decision <5 ms, tactical <20 ms"; brief 06: "never wait for model or dashboard", acceptance "p99/max latency". SHARED_CONTRACTS.md:527: "publish every record of the step to the journal before the next input". journal.py:217 defaults to fsync per record; publish() encodes each record three times (to_wire at :170, fingerprint at :172, entry.to_wire() in _persist at :274 - the `wire` argument is unused), and RecordSink has no step-level commit. Measured on the review container (Xeon 2.1 GHz, Python 3.13.18, labelled fixtures, two runs, machine shared with other jobs - not evidence about the owner's hardware): FileJournal(fsync=True).publish(Tick) p50 0.33-0.57 ms, p99 1.0-1.6 ms; publish(Position) p50 0.65-0.74 ms, p99 1.6-1.9 ms; without fsync p50 0.11 ms and 0.29-0.32 ms; MemoryJournal 0.09 ms and 0.15-0.26 ms; one stop tightening (two OrderEvents built, gateway.replace, poll, no journal) p50 0.21-0.22 ms, p99 0.4-0.5 ms. A tick with one open position whose stop is ratcheted journals four records, about 2 ms p50 with fsync before any reflex logic, linear in open positions. Reopening a FileJournal replays every record through all checks at 0.33-0.40 ms per record (about 6 minutes per million records, during which nothing is monitored) and the journal retains every record in memory (891 bytes per journaled tick, about 0.9 GB per million ticks); LifecycleLedger keeps every order and open_orders() scans all of them. ARCHITECTURE.md section 10 admits cost was measured on synthetic records only; tools/benchmark_foundation.py times publish(tick) alone.
findings.proposed_change: Add a step-level commit to RecordSink (publish_many or commit(), one fsync per step), reuse the canonical bytes for fingerprint and file line, decide whether raw ticks belong in the run journal at all (the tick store holds them; journal a reference), define the Position cadence, add checkpoints so a restart replays from the last snapshot, and evict terminal chains from the ledger. Extend the foundation benchmark with a per-step budget case (N open positions, ratchet on every tick) reported against the proposed targets.

findings.area: Routing lock layer 4 / adapter registration (S07-ACC-07, S07-ASG-16, G08-10)
findings.title: The static live-lock scan is referenced everywhere but absent, and the adapter allow-list trusts a self-declared module name
findings.detail: Master: "Paper/replay only; build execution interfaces but keep real order routing disabled." Brief 07 acceptance: "no real orders". core/routing_lock.py:21-23 and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:134 describe tools/check_live_lock.py "(run in CI)"; tools/ci.py:75-78 runs `python -m tools.check_live_lock`, and further steps run tools.check_architecture, tools.check_docs_paths and tools.check_no_secrets. At HEAD 0e52f3f (labelled WIP) none of these modules exists (tools/ holds benchmark_foundation, build_review, ci, gie_registers, make_file_manifest, make_golden, render_contract_docs, summarize_reviews), nor tests/gie/tools/test_check_live_lock.py named in specifications/acceptance_tests.yaml:56; dispositions SF-01, SF-05 ("scan rule LL011"), SF-18 and SF-24 name them as the fix. routing_lock.py:161-168 checks adapter_type.__module__, an attribute any code can set. Run from a scratch script outside the repository: type('Spoof', (), {'__module__': 'gie.execution.not_a_real_module', ...}) is registered by register_simulated_adapter although that module is not in sys.modules; the fake adapter used for this review was registered the same way under 'tests.review_fake_adapter'. Tests for LifecycleLedger, GuardedExecutionAdapter, the journal and the authorisation checks were not in the tree at that commit (contract tests were being added to the working tree while this review ran).
findings.proposed_change: Deliver the scan with its tests before the review gate, or mark SF-01 / SF-05 / SF-18 / SF-24 as open and say so in routing_lock.py and ARCHITECTURE.md. In register_simulated_adapter require that sys.modules[module] exists, that its file lies under the allow-listed package directory and that getattr(module, qualname) is the class being registered; admit the 'tests.' prefix only when a test fixture enables it.

findings.area: Simulated venue semantics shared by 06, 07 and 10 (S07-ASG-11, S07-ASG-13, S07-ACC-08, S07-DEL-03)
findings.title: Trigger side, slippage limit and the order of broker and reflex inside a step are not stated
findings.detail: Brief 07: "Model bid/ask, costs, slippage, latency and broker constraints"; acceptance "deterministic replay"; deliverable "execution parity". OrderEvent.trigger_price is documented only as "Stop trigger price" (order_event.py:295-297) without saying which quote triggers it, while reference_price is defined per side (:298-302). TradePlan.max_spread and max_entry_slippage (trade_plan.py:275-282) have no counterpart on the order, and the adapter receives only the OrderEvent (interfaces.py:145), so a broker-side slippage limit cannot be modelled. validate_entry_authorization does not relate attached_take_profit_price to the plan's targets. SHARED_CONTRACTS.md:526 lists "protective (reflex, simulated broker)" without saying whether the broker processes the tick before the reflex engine (a stop hit by tick N is then already filled when reflex decides) or after it.
findings.proposed_change: State normatively: STOP and LIMIT orders are evaluated on the executable side (SELL against bid, BUY against ask). Add max_slippage (price distance) to OrderEvent for MARKET and STOP entries, copied from the plan and checked by validate_entry_authorization. Fix the order simulated broker -> reflex inside the protective phase. Bind attached_take_profit_price to one of plan.targets.

findings.area: Position fields needed by the reflex engine (S06-ASG-05, S06-ASG-07, G01)
findings.title: Position lacks what the reflex engine needs to act without lookups
findings.detail: Brief 06: "trade-health reactions ... never wait for model or dashboard"; master G01: "overnight positions when permitted and monitored, no weekend exposure". Position (position.py:112-200) has no reference to its working PROTECTIVE_STOP order (the reflex engine must guess the attempt number or scan ledger.open_orders()), a single take_profit_price although a plan has up to eight targets with close fractions (trade_plan.py:245-255), and no overnight_allowed or time limit; those are on TradePlan, which SHARED_CONTRACTS.md:32 does not deliver to 06, and Candidate.expected_holding_time_ns reaches neither the plan nor the position.
findings.proposed_change: Add protective_client_order_id, overnight_allowed and the remaining exit schedule (targets with close fractions) to Position as immutable copies from the plan at opening, or list 06 as a TradePlan consumer and add a ledger lookup by plan_id.

findings.area: Exact fractions at the daily boundaries (S08-ACC-01..05, G05-08)
findings.title: Daily fractions cannot be computed exactly for an arbitrary reference equity, and only risk_frac has a rounding rule
findings.detail: SHARED_CONTRACTS.md:81-87: fractions in risk-limit comparisons are exact decimals under EXACT "so that boundary rules such as 'at exactly the floor no new risk' (G05-08) are decided exactly"; brief 08 acceptance: "Boundary tests at -2%, proposed -1.75%, -3%, +5%; exact-floor no new risk". Run: EXACT.divide(104.00, 100000) = 0.00104, but EXACT.divide(104.00, 99987.33) raises decimal.Inexact, and a risk_frac with 13 fractional digits is refused by the field. risk_decision.py:78-80 defines rounding up for risk_frac only; daily_pnl_frac and profit_floor_frac have no direction, RiskDecision carries no daily P&L amount or floor amount, and gie.core.canonical has no rounding helper, so 08, QA and the dashboard can disagree exactly at the tested boundaries.
findings.proposed_change: Add daily_pnl_amount and profit_floor_amount (exact money) and decide the boundaries on amounts. Define the fractions as derived values with a stated direction (P&L towards minus infinity, floor and risk up, 12 fractional digits) and provide one helper in gie.core.canonical used by every session.

findings.area: RiskDecision as evidence of the risk rules (G04-02, G04-03, G04-08, G04-09, S08-ASG-12, G05-13)
findings.title: RiskDecision cannot evidence several rules that brief 08 makes the risk engine responsible for
findings.detail: Master G04: "aggregate gross/net and correlated risk ... Adaptive sizing only from validated quality; no martingale"; brief 08: "No risk increase to recover losses"; G05: "defensive at -2%, reduced risk and stricter quality". open_risk_amount is "Aggregate risk of open positions" (risk_decision.py:151-155) without saying gross or net; there is no exposure or correlated-risk field and no baseline size against which 'reduced' or 'increased' could be read. Runs: an APPROVED (not reduced) decision in DEFENSIVE at pnl -0.025 constructs, and so does NORMAL at -0.05. 'Quality' has no carrier on the plan the gate receives: quality_score exists only on Candidate, which 08 does not consume (SHARED_CONTRACTS.md:31).
findings.proposed_change: Add gross_exposure_lots, net_exposure_lots, correlated_risk_amount (nullable until defined by 08), base_risk_frac (size before adaptation) and the quality value that was used. State which plan field is 'quality' for G04-08 or carry the candidate's quality_score on TradePlan.

findings.area: RunManifest / FileJournal - replay determinism and unattended restart (S07-ACC-08, S07-ACC-05, G08-01)
findings.title: Two replays of the same configuration do not produce the same journal bytes, and a torn tail stops an unattended restart
findings.detail: SHARED_CONTRACTS.md:349: "Replaying the same inputs MUST reproduce the journal byte for byte (S01-ACC-08, S07-ACC-08, S10-ACC-01)." run.py:103-105: RunManifest.created_time_ns is "system clock, also for replays" and is not part of run_id. Run: two manifests of the same configuration created one second apart have the same run_id, the two journals are not byte-identical (line 0 differs), and publishing the second manifest into the first journal raises SequenceConflictError 'a journal belongs to exactly one run'. Separately, journal.py:234-238 refuses to open a journal with an incomplete last line until an operator calls repair_torn_tail (run: JournalCorruptError; repair removed 41 bytes; reopen succeeded with the open order restored), while master G08 asks for an "autonomous order lifecycle foundation ... restart reconciliation ... overnight monitoring".
findings.proposed_change: For REPLAY take created_time_ns from the run configuration (or exclude it from the byte comparison and say so in section 6.2). Let the run loop remove a torn tail automatically at start-up and journal that it did so (the torn record was never published); keep the refusal for every other kind of damage.
